item.title: Binance Says Crypto Is Still OK. It Really Is Not
item.description: The digital-asset industry has just suffered the biggest heist in its brief history with the $6.3 billion hacking of Binance, the No. 1 crypto platform. Yet the messaging from the top is that things are going to be A-OK.
item.dc:creator: Lionel Laurent

item.title: Alaska Ballot Shenanigans Could Hurt Peltola, Help Dan Sullivan
item.description: Like Claude Rains in the classic film “Casablanca,” Republicans from President Donald Trump on down were shocked, shocked, by the bombshell New York Times report this week that the campaign of Alaska Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola schemed to recruit a retired schoolteacher named Dan J. Sullivan into her race against Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan. (Peltola herself has denied she knew of the effort.)
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Microsoft and Skydance Buyouts Show Different Approaches to Job Cuts
item.description: Has the era of the mega-layoff come to an end, replaced by the start of the more humane “buyout boom”? That’s how announcements from Microsoft Corp. and Skydance Corp. offering employees voluntary exits on the same day are being interpreted.
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: Video Gamers Hate AI But It May Help Reduce Billion Dollar Budgets
item.description: Aficionados want better graphics and effects, but the gaming industry is reaching billion-dollar budgets that artificial intelligence might help reduce.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: What If the Problem Is Too Much Capital?
item.description: It needs to go somewhere, from imperial adventures to AI.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Amazon Earnings: Jassy Has a Trillion-Dollar AWS in His Sights
item.description: Similar to investor reaction to Alphabet Inc.’s earnings a day earlier, the stellar performance of Amazon.com Inc.’s cloud unit was overshadowed by jitters around other parts of the business when the company reported third-quarter results on Thursday. A softer-than-expected forecast for Christmas and a miss on quarterly revenue prompted a sharp selloff after hours. At one point shares were down 7% after dropping 4.25% earlier in the day.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: AI's Coming Dystopia Was Skewered 300 Years Ago by Jonathan Swift
item.description: It takes a rare genius to write a satire that is still read 300 years after its publication. Most satire dwells on the peccadilloes of soon-to-be forgotten politicians. And it takes a unique genius to write a satire that is more relevant today than it was in the days of powdered wigs and knee breeches. That is exactly what Jonathan Swift achieved when he published Gulliver’s Travels Into Remote Regions of the World on Oct. 28, 1726.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Halloween Candy Tamed The Holiday Maybe a Little Too Well
item.description: It’s that time of year when toddlers, tweens and even some teens will go door to door, sacks outstretched for candy. While they’ll mumble “trick or treat,” tricks are few and far between these days.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Mihm

item.title: AI Labs’ Cybersecurity Gains Come at the Economy’s Expense
item.description: Last week programmers raced to fix flaws that have been known for years in a programming language that is itself more than three decades old. Why the rush? Because the language, called PHP, is used by about a billion websites worldwide, and the defects would allow an attacker to take over a web server. OpenAI, whose models helped discover the vulnerabilities, called them “one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.”
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda
